topomer.note: 29 of 111 molecules can be cut at the framework

findings.text: 57 chemotype(s); the largest holds 20 of 111 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 24 heavy atoms, about 89% of a typical molecule, and 26% of the set can be cut at it
the 24 shared framework atoms sit 0.2 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (46 of 111 carry them)
the aligned model is +0.364 in q2 against counts (95% interval +0.237 to +0.499) -- the frame does better than counts
the aligned model is +0.024 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.173 to +0.236) -- the frame gains nothing over invariant
the aligned model is -0.048 in q2 against topomer (95% interval -0.305 to +0.122) -- cutting the molecules and posing the pieces by rule does as well as the frame, on the molecules that can be cut
the aligned model is +0.294 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval +0.128 to +0.479) -- the geometry adds something

why: the frame gains nothing over invariant, which needs no alignment to curate and cannot be done wrongly
